name: streamlink-c3c2e98c-blind26-v1-ots
instr:
# Repairing 26 undocumented behaviour regressions in a command-line video downloader without a test suite

A utility that fetches live and on-demand video from a great many sites, hands it to a player or saves it to disk, is now getting a lot of small things wrong at once. The repository has received 26 separate undocumented edits. Everything below was seen in ordinary use; nothing else is known about where the changes sit.

Several of them show up right at the terminal, in what gets printed and in how a run ends. Asking it to print which address patterns a named site handler accepts still prints them, but the note marking entries whose priority is unusual is now attached to exactly the wrong ones: entries with the ordinary priority carry the note and the genuinely unusual ones have lost it, so the printed block is wrong whether the handler was loaded lazily or eagerly. Asking for the patterns of a name nobody knows prints the same not-found text as before, but the process exits with status 2 where it used to exit with 1. Giving it both a destination to write to and a request to record is now accepted silently and the run proceeds, and the same holds for a destination together with record-and-pipe; each combination used to be refused outright with an error message and exit status 1.
